title: Concurrent surge fallback policy and post-incident action catalog
creator: Ethan Park
description: Synthesize the recent dedicated-capacity shortfall incident into a compact playbook: create an explicit concurrent-surge fallback policy, enumerate automated mitigations, and produce an actionable catalog of post-incident items for engineering and SRE. Deliverables: fallback policy (policy + automated guardrail), updated runbook, prioritized action catalog with owners and timeline.
summary: After the March 8th surge that caused a 12-minute headroom collapse for multiple Dedicated pools, we need a durable fallback policy that triggers deterministic capacity-preserving actions and a catalog of post-incident tasks to close gaps identified by RCA.
impact: Several high-volume customers experienced degraded throughput and increased tail latency; some requests were routed to lower-capacity model variants leading to quality degradations for affected routes.
rca: Primary cause: an orchestration regression that allowed concurrent scale-in and placement churn during a global autoscale event, producing transient pod allocation delays.
Secondary cause: headroom calculations relied on a single metric (active_slots_available) which underreported usable capacity when KV cache warmup caused bursty allocation demand.
Contributing factor: no deterministic fallback policy to limit non-critical routes during capacity pressure, leading to noisy neighbor effects across tenant pools.
Detection lag: alert thresholds for dedicated-pool-headroom were tuned for steady-state and did not capture rapid slope change; monitoring gaps in 95th-99th minute-series contributed to late paging.
timeline: 2026-03-08 02:13 UTC: surge begins; autoscaler triggers scale-out but several placement operations overlap with scale-in windows.
2026-03-08 02:15 UTC: first alert - dedicated-pool-headroom < 10% for pool-us-west-4-a.
2026-03-08 02:25 UTC: mitigation - on-call manually increased pool reserve and enabled emergency burst nodes; partial recovery by 02:36 UTC.
2026-03-08 03:00 UTC: incident declared resolved, but follow-up investigation initiated for root causes and mitigation gaps.
action_items: (Priya) Draft concurrent-surge fallback policy that: 1) ratelimits low-priority routes, 2) pins critical latencies to reserved headroom, 3) triggers model-variant fallback only after retry budget exhaustion - due 2026-03-21
(Samir) Implement autoscaler guard that prevents concurrent scale-in during pending placement operations (mutex at placement controller) - due 2026-03-28
(Aisha) Update headroom metric to include KV-cache-adjusted capacity and add 1m and 5m slope detectors to alerting - due 2026-03-18
(Infra) Add synthetic soak tests that simulate KV-warmup bursts and verify headroom calculations on every runtime build - due 2026-04-04
(SRE) Improve runbook to include emergency throttle commands, quick reallocation play, and an automated escalation path to capacity ops - due 2026-03-17
(PM) Prioritize top three customers for post-incident outreach and provide mitigation summary and ETA for fixes - due 2026-03-20
notes: We intentionally avoid model evictions as first line fallback because that leads to user-visible quality regressions; prefer route-level throttles and reserve enforcement.
Consider temporary admission-control tokens for high-value customers to preserve SLAs during incidents.
Long-term: explore predictive autoscaler that uses request-pattern clustering to avoid simultaneous placement churn.

decisions: Do not perform user-visible model variant fallback unless automated fallback budget is exhausted and fallback is accompanied by a quality regression note in logs.
Primary emergency action is route-level throttling and reserve enforcement; autoscaler guardrails prevent placement churn before scaling decisions are applied.
Create a lightweight 'incident sprint' with 3 owners for the highest-priority fixes; all fixes to be code-reviewed within 72 hours.
Expose a customer-facing incident summary template for Dedicated customers to improve transparency.
